newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ANDORRAN AMATEURS GET EIGHT-GOAL THRASHING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANDORRAN AMATEURS GET EIGHT-GOAL THRASHING.

text.p: Club Esportiu Principat, from Andorra, got a rude introduction to European soccer with an 8-0 thrashing by Scottish visitors Dundee United on Wednesday.
The club, who until recently were known as Charlie's Restaurant and who were made up of local Real Madrid supporters, had talked jokingly about keeping the scoreline in single figures.
The amateur team, made up of a mixture of bricklayers, van drivers, a travel agent and a driving school instructor, held out for 13 minutes before Robbie Winters got Dundee United's opening goal.
The hosts, who were given no chance against the experienced Scottish side who have played in Europe on 21 previous occasions, then proved surprisingly resilient for the rest of the first half.
A bad mistake by goalkeeper Rui Castro after 30 minutes, when he let a shot by Winters from 20 metres slip through his hands, was their only other slip up.
Castro even went some way to redeeming himself when he saved a penalty by Erik Pederson a minute before the break.
But any dreams the Andorrans had of keeping the deficit respectably low, on a clear night in the Pyrenees, were dashed in a miserable second half.
Goals from second half substitute Gary McSwegan and Swedish midfielder Lars Zetterlund in the first five minutes after the restart made the score 4-0.
A four goal flurry in just four minutes meant Andorran ambitions of progressing further in the UEFA Cup were completely eradicated.
McSwegan got his second goal after 73 minutes and Winters put Dundee's sixth past the hapless Castro two minutes later.
McSwegan scored yet again after 76 minutes and Winters got his fourth after 77 minutes.
Nevertheless the Andorrans were far from discouraged after their first experience of European soccer after only being allowed into the UEFA Cup in May.
"Overall, I'd have to say we are quite happy," said the CE Principat coach Andres Zapata.
"We only let in two goals in the first half. And if you can forget the actual goals, I thought we played well."
